title: Projects
text:

title: Projects
section: Manufacturing Time-Series Analytics in NSF-Funded Research
text:
Manufacturing Time-Series Analytics in NSF-Funded Research
This work contributed to NSF-funded research on manufacturing analytics at West Virginia University. The project emphasized rigorous experimental evaluation of algorithms for manufacturing time-series data and practical guidance for selecting methods in smart manufacturing applications.
Methods: benchmark design, experimental evaluation, manufacturing datasets, statistical and machine learning models, deep learning architectures.
Contribution: led the manufacturing time-series analytics task and helped define how forecasting and classification algorithms can be assessed for industrial use cases.
Related outputs: journal publications in Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing, Journal of Manufacturing Systems, and Manufacturing Letters.

title: Projects
section: Real-Time Defect Detection in Robotic Assembly
text:
Real-Time Defect Detection in Robotic Assembly
This project applies machine learning to real-time defect detection and classification in robotic assembly lines. The goal is to connect sensor-rich robotic assembly data with fast quality assessment and actionable process feedback.
Methods: supervised machine learning, feature extraction, classification, real-time monitoring, robotic assembly data analysis.
Contribution: contributed to an ML framework for detecting and classifying defects during robotic assembly operations.
Related output: Real-time defect detection and classification in robotic assembly lines: A machine learning framework.

title: Projects
section: Federated Learning and Blockchain for Smart Manufacturing
text:
Federated Learning and Blockchain for Smart Manufacturing
This project explores secure collaborative AI for manufacturing systems where organizations may need to learn from distributed data without exposing sensitive operational information.
Methods: federated learning, blockchain, deep learning for time-series forecasting, privacy-preserving analytics, collaborative manufacturing systems.
Contribution: investigates how federated learning and blockchain can support trustworthy model training and coordination across distributed manufacturing partners.
Related outputs: publications on federated learning for smart manufacturing and blockchain-empowered federated learning applications.

title: Projects
section: Rocket Assembly Line Testbed as a Service
text:
Rocket Assembly Line Testbed as a Service
This project studies data acquisition strategies and testbed-as-a-service models for rocket assembly lines. The work supports repeatable experimentation, data collection, and analytics development for complex manufacturing systems.
Methods: testbed design, data acquisition, manufacturing systems engineering, experimental infrastructure, assembly-line analytics.
Contribution: contributed to the comparison of data acquisition strategies and the design of a testbed-as-a-service framework for manufacturing analytics research.
Related output: Rocket assembly line testbed as a service (TaaS): A comparison of data acquisition strategies.

title: Projects
section: Agentic AI and Multi-Agent Systems in Smart Manufacturing
text:
Agentic AI and Multi-Agent Systems in Smart Manufacturing
This project investigates how agentic AI and multi-agent systems can support decision-making in smart manufacturing. The work focuses on coordinating autonomous or semi-autonomous agents for diagnosis, planning, maintenance, and system-level decision support.
Methods: agentic AI, multi-agent systems, industrial AI, smart manufacturing decision support.
Contribution: frames the role of agent-based intelligence in manufacturing systems and identifies opportunities for hybrid human-AI and multi-agent workflows.
Related output: Hybrid agentic AI and multi-agent systems in smart manufacturing.

title: Projects
section: Digital Twin Enabled Robot Collision Detection
text:
Digital Twin Enabled Robot Collision Detection
This project connects digital twins, robot monitoring, and time-series forecasting to detect and anticipate collision-related behavior in robotic systems.
Methods: digital twins, robot analytics, time-series forecasting, collision detection, predictive monitoring.
Contribution: contributed to a digital twin enabled approach for robot collision detection using time-series forecasting methods.
Related output: Digital twin enabled robot collision detection using time series forecasting.

title: Research
text:
My research develops data-driven and AI-enabled methods for smart manufacturing systems. I work at the intersection of industrial engineering, time-series analytics, machine learning, deep learning, and collaborative manufacturing intelligence, with an emphasis on methods that can support real manufacturing decisions.
The central goal of my work is to help manufacturing systems use data more effectively: to forecast system behavior, classify events, detect quality issues, support predictive maintenance, coordinate distributed decision-making, and improve resilience across production and supply-network environments.

title: Research
text:
Core Questions

How can manufacturing time-series data be transformed into reliable decision support?
How should AI and machine learning algorithms be evaluated for industrial use rather than only benchmark performance?
How can deep learning models support forecasting, classification, predictive maintenance, and quality improvement in real manufacturing systems?
How can federated learning and blockchain support secure collaborative analytics across organizations?
How can agentic AI, multi-agent systems, and digital twins support smart manufacturing operations?

title: Research
text:
Research Themes

Time-Series Analytics for Smart Manufacturing
Manufacturing systems generate high-frequency, multivariate, and heterogeneous time-series data. My work studies forecasting, classification, anomaly detection, and pattern recognition methods that help translate these streams into process insight and operational decisions.
Related work includes research on time-series forecasting, time-series classification, high-resolution classification, and time-series pattern recognition in smart manufacturing systems.


Industrial AI and Machine Learning
I apply machine learning to manufacturing problems such as process monitoring, predictive maintenance, quality prediction, and defect detection. This includes both model development and experimental evaluation of algorithms in realistic industrial settings.
This theme connects to projects on real-time defect detection, robotic assembly, directed energy deposition additive manufacturing, and hybrid physics-based/data-driven modeling.


Deep Learning for Manufacturing Analytics
My research uses deep learning for forecasting, classification, predictive maintenance, and quality improvement. I am interested in models that can handle temporal dependencies, noisy measurements, and changing manufacturing conditions.
Current work includes deep learning architectures for manufacturing time-series forecasting and classification, including collaborative settings where data is distributed across partners.


Agentic AI and Multi-Agent Systems
I study Agentic AI and multi-agent systems for decision support in manufacturing. This includes exploring how autonomous and semi-autonomous agents can support diagnosis, planning, maintenance, and coordination across complex production environments.
This direction examines how agent-based intelligence can complement human expertise and existing industrial systems.


Digital Twins and Digital Supply Networks
Digital twins and digital supply networks can connect physical operations with analytical models, simulation, and system-level visibility. My work explores how these technologies can support manufacturing resilience, collaboration, and performance improvement.
Related work includes digital twin enabled robot monitoring and time-series forecasting for collision detection.


Federated Learning and Blockchain for Secure Collaboration
I study privacy-preserving and trustworthy collaborative AI frameworks for smart manufacturing. This includes federated learning and blockchain-enabled approaches for sharing model intelligence across organizations without exposing sensitive manufacturing data.
This theme supports a broader research direction in secure digital supply networks and collaborative manufacturing analytics.

title: Research
text:
Current Directions

Agentic AI for smart manufacturing: studying how agentic AI and multi-agent systems can support planning, diagnosis, coordination, and decision support.
Secure collaborative manufacturing analytics: integrating federated learning, blockchain, and deep learning for privacy-preserving industrial AI.
Digital twins and robotic systems: using time-series forecasting and digital twin models for robot monitoring and collision detection.
Practical AI/ML guidance for industry: developing applied guidance for manufacturing organizations adopting time-series analytics, machine learning, and deep learning.

See the Projects page for selected applications and the Publications page for related papers.

title: Mojtaba A. Farahani
text:
I am a postdoctoral researcher at the University of South Carolina working on data-driven analytics for smart manufacturing systems. My research develops AI-enabled methods for understanding, forecasting, and improving complex manufacturing systems through time-series analytics, machine learning, deep learning, digital twins, and collaborative industrial intelligence.
My work focuses on practical analytics for process optimization, quality improvement, predictive maintenance, robotics and assembly, and secure collaborative manufacturing systems. I am especially interested in methods that connect data-rich manufacturing environments with trustworthy decision support.
